steps.content:
10:00, November 25, N.F. 113
The Exiles' Base
More and more people are coming to seek refuge. Amid the gloom and doom, there are still a few occasional delights to brighten up the atmosphere at the base.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: New Yooga! Infuse yourself with the energy of the sun, brighter and healthier than ever!

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: Come on, practice with me!
Though it doesn't usually last very long.
(Scene change)

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: Phew... There are a lot of newcomers lately and they're all coming to me for health advice. My back is about to give out...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: The Executive Committee's recent moves are terrorizing people, so they are more inclined to join us.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: Are you talking about the census and resettlement? Hmm... From my Outlander perspective, relocation is somewhat acceptable.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: Compared to waiting for death under the Black Ring, obeying the orders and moving to the satellite towns with everyone else doesn't sound that bad.

The city-state relocates its population to the abandoned satellite towns, then cuts off the hypercube supply under the guise of a fake accident. This way, these burdens will sooner or later disappear in one of the Tides of Ashes. Population management or resettlement is just another name for the Purge Order.
A few small figures walk in, tightening their cloaks, followed by several newly joined refugees.
Similar rumors are heard everywhere lately, scaring many out of their wits. A few weeks ago, they were indifferent to us, but now they're desperately begging to come.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Welcome back, Ica. None of those rumors has been confirmed. Don't repeat them, it'll only make people afraid.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: It's all thanks to the Homeless helping to spread the word that we've been able to recruit so many people. You guys have done a great job.
Ica glances at Matilda.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Save your flattery. You're already here, yet you still wear that Executive Officer uniform. You enjoy sticking out like a sore thumb?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: This outfit makes it easier for people to find me. Besides, not everyone thinks I'm an eyesore.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Tsk, like I trust you. Where's Crache?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: She's at the usual place.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: I'll go find her.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Also, I brought back those eye drops. It's on your desk. You were complaining that you ran out last time, right?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: I completely forgot about it. It's not easy to find outside the Executive Committee. Did you actually get it for me? Thank you.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: I just passed by SALVA and they insisted I take it! The Homeless are very busy, there won't be a next time!!
Before Matilda can respond, the kid runs off in a puff of smoke.

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: ...So the SALVA doctors are back too. I must arrange a visit soon. We need their strength.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: Pfft, that's not the point. That kid Ica actually cares about you now, huh? Does joining the Homeless turn these kids into big softies or what?

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Ica knows that information from Eastside is crucial, that's why he swallows his anger and tries to talk to me. He's very smart.

Matilda has looked into it. Ica's parents died in the Executive Committee's detention center last year and he joined Rustfire to avenge his parents. He's only tolerating the existence of an Eastsider Executive Officer for a greater goal.

Too many children here were forced to grow up prematurely. What was Matilda like when she was their age? What kind of life do the children of Eastside lead? Everything here is different from Eastside, then...

steps.speaker: Matilda
steps.content: Will I find the answers to the questions that the past me couldn't answer here?
[Scene Change] Raven's Office

Crache spends a lot of time out fighting that her dark circles are getting worse. The people of the refugee camp decided to give her a private room. When Crache first heard this suggestion, she was silent for a long time, and finally asked for the room where Raven's works are stored in.
These days, whenever she's free, she flips through her poems, diary, investigative report, or something like that. But there aren't many left.
Her shadow shudders, and Crache closes the notebook in her hands with a snap and shoves it into the drawer. The door opens.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Boss, I'm back. Reading Raye's notes again?
Crache's eyelid twitches. She says nothing, but Ica doesn't notice her unusual reaction and simply pulls out a flyer from his backpack excitedly.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Check this out! I've got a rousing poem by Raven. It's brilliantly written, full of strength.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: We've copied stacks and stacks of it at night with kids at the base and distributed them everywhere during the day. It's effective publicity!

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Don't...
Crache opens her mouth to stop him from reciting it, but it's too late. Ica clears his throat and begins...

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content:
Ahem! In this darkest night, those who stay silent await the end, those who hesitate are doomed to fail, and those who cower live on with regrets.
But those of you who merely miss the glimmer in the dark and lose your way in the fog, come with me...

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: The pitch-black Raven has pitch-black eyes. With them, I shall find the light and return it to you!

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Now, look up and listen closely...

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: If winter comes, can spring be far behind?
An ominous echo makes Crache shiver. This is undoubtedly the flamboyant style of the Rustfire poet. She has successfully poisoned the minds of a few Syndican children as she wished.
The sheets are covered in childish, wiggly handwriting. These are the pamphlets the children of the base have spent nights copying. Crache remembers the hundreds of wordless books left by Raven.
The one who always boasted about the tens of thousands of poems she'd written. After that great battle, all she left behind was a room full of blank sheets and the inkless imprints on them.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: The shackles' contamination has slowed down her body's recovery. When Donald carried her here, it freaked me out, but she's still hanging on.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Looking on the bright side, now she's only half-dead, at least she can still pass on messages to Oak Casket. Rustfire's liaison and top spy holds so much valuable information that has proven useful, right?

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: Hmm... Don't worry, she won't die so easily. Oak Casket insists that I wake her up. She finds her too loud and bothersome. As soon as Raven wakes up, we'll ask you to come take her back at once.

steps.speaker: Dudu
steps.content: It may take a while, but once ${PlayerName} wakes up and the problem with the shackles gets sorted out, I suppose everything will be fine...
Thinking of this, Crache's expression dims. She shoves the flyer back into Ica's hand.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...Copy as many as you like, but don't spend all day distributing this kind of thing on the streets with the kids. It's dangerous out there.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: The Executive Committee is watching. Besides, given what Rustfire has become, no one believes their words anymore. Distributing these flyers will only make it worse.
Though Ica admires Crache, the boy still can't help but feel a bit indignant. He thought his hard effort at least deserved some praise from his leader.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: But I did bring a lot of people back. Even that Executive Officer lady gave us credit.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: The newcomers were just scared by the rumors of the Purge Order. No one in Syndicate would take the words of a kid seriously.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: But everyone calls you the Guardian out there... What you're saying doesn't even sound convincing...
Crache is speechless. She turns around, finds a medical kit, and throws it to Ica. The boy tries his best to hide his wounds, but nothing escapes his boss.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: I've never managed to protect anything. There is no Guardian in this world. Even if there were... It can die too.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: If you must flaunt the Homeless' name, then be careful out there. Don't put your life at risk for something stupid.
The boy doesn't pick up on the complex emotions in her words, but he does catch the boss's indirect concern for him. He rubs his nose and smiles.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: I'm being careful. I'm not a kid anymore. I can protect myself, and I can do a lot of things now.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Those guys from the Executive Committee always say West District is rotten and deserves this. They say that Rustfire kidnapped and killed ${PlayerName}. Bunch of liars! It was ${PlayerName} who chose to stay and fight with us, and Rustfire sacrificed an entire squad to save him.
steps.female_content: Those guys from the Executive Committee always say West District is rotten and deserves this. They say that Rustfire kidnapped and killed ${PlayerName}. Bunch of liars! It was ${PlayerName} who chose to stay and fight with us, and Rustfire sacrificed an entire squad to save her.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: But I won't just sit there and sulk anymore. We've taken a lot of photos and videos and posted them online. Eastsiders are seeing them, and finally, some are speaking up for us. The suffering of children attracts more attention, right?

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Those on the other side of the Rust are people too, and some of them must be good. I believe not all of them have the heart to support the Purge Order.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: This is what Raven meant by taking advantage of public opinion, right? Rustfire's work will not be in vain!

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: Who knows? Stay alive, and when she wakes up, you can ask her yourself. You two have more in common.
At that moment, the shadow on the ground quivers. Ica distinctly sees the previous dejection vanish from his boss's gaze and her eyes are now sharp as a warrior's.
Immediately, they hear shrill screams from outside. Crache follows the shadow and rushes out.

steps.speaker: Crache
steps.content: ...I'll go, you stay here.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: Hmph, I thought you didn't care.
Ica thinks to himself and follows. He's certain he's glimpsed the real leader of the Homeless in those eyes.

steps.speaker: Ica
steps.content: No, I'm going too!
Meanwhile, the refugee camp's emergency room is in a shambles.

steps.speaker: Greta
steps.content: It's Mania! The newly arrived patient is infected with Mania!
